summary: Teams conduct a simulated business meeting using parliamentary procedure, demonstrating leadership, correct meeting management, and professional decorum. The event includes a parliamentary demonstration, an oral examination, and an objective test. Teams are evaluated on their ability to apply Robert’s Rules of Order, process motions, communicate clearly, and record accurate minutes.
time_limits: No more than fifteen (15) minutes preparation time
No more than fifteen (15) minutes parliamentary demonstration
No more than five (5) minutes judges’ questions
submission_requirements: Secretary’s handwritten notes and contest agenda submitted to judges immediately after the presentation
what_to_bring: Robert’s Rules of Order Newly Revised (current edition)
Sharpened pencils, pens for secretary’s minutes
Published and/or unpublished reference materials in the preparation room only
Opening and Closing a Meeting scripts in the preparation room only
competencies: Demonstrate accurate knowledge of parliamentary procedures and apply the rules correctly during a meeting
Apply democratic principles to ensure fair, orderly, and inclusive decision-making
Conduct or participate in a structured business meeting using proper procedures, agendas, and meeting etiquette
Correctly process, state, handle, and dispose of assigned parliamentary motions, demonstrating proper use of debate, precedence, and voting procedures
Manage time effectively to keep the meeting progressing efficiently and within required limits
Work effectively as a team by assigning roles, collaborating respectfully, and supporting a smooth and efficient meeting demonstration
Communicate clearly and professionally when stating motions, presenting arguments, and debating, using effective verbal and nonverbal delivery skills
Interpret and follow an agenda to maintain proper meeting flow and sequencing of business
Demonstrate professional conduct and meeting etiquette, showing respect for members, officers, and the decision-making process
Record clear, accurate, and essential meeting minutes in real time, following basic RONR guidelines

judging_notes: All team members must take an objective parliamentary procedure test. The test should be administered to all team members at the same time. The average score will be added to the team score.
The test is specific to this event. Reference materials are NOT allowed.
Suggested resource for objective portion: Dunbar’s Manual of Parliamentary Procedure
Finals may be part of the competition
Judge questions will be directed to the Chairperson for any contestant to answer. Questions from the judges will have reference to the abilities demonstrated during the event.
Judges’ comments will be returned digitally through the online judging system at the national level.
eligibility_notes: Any secondary division contestant may enter this team event.
Each state is allowed three (3) entries.
Contestants who participate in this event at the national level are eligible for twelve (12) years of paid membership offered by the American Institute of Parliamentarians.
